name: validator
tagline: Author validation once in Go. Run it everywhere.
description: Struct-native Go validator whose rules are a serializable IR: the same rules validate in Go (zero-alloc codegen), export to JSON Schema, and generate a Standard-Schema-compatible TypeScript validator. Non-portable rules are reported, never silently dropped.

positioning.audience: Go backend teams with a TypeScript frontend who are tired of maintaining the same validation rules twice
positioning.problem: every Go validator either stores rules as opaque closures or tag strings that cannot be exported, so frontend validation is hand-copied and drifts; the one tool that exports (Tygor) silently drops custom rules
differentiators: rules are serializable data, not closures
one IR feeds Go validation, JSON Schema, and TS generation in lockstep
codegen zero-alloc hot path with a reflection fallback
explicit portability manifest — non-portable rules are never dropped
Standard Schema output drops into tRPC/TanStack/RHF adapter-free
